_comment: marble_spikes, ROUND: a placeable patch of the marble rotunda's spike floor. A hexagonal slab 2.50 m across the corners (r 1.25) and 0.10 m thick, six cells round a small bare hub, one spike stitched into each -- the pit's own pedestal-ring-and-pyramid cell (marble_lane_build), the pit's taper (marble_build.BASE_K) and its small spike at every third foot, cones 1.2..2.2 m tall on a 0.12 m plinth: the tallest tip is at y 2.22. ORIGIN IS THE BASE CENTRE and y=0 is the floor it sits on, so the scene drops it at the walkway's own height and nothing else. ONE material: marble_build's painted 256 px atlas, zones field/spike/plinth/shade. HAZARD, NOT COVER -- MarbleSpikesCollision is the SLAB ONLY, a closed hexagonal prism r 1.25 x 0.10 m shipped as a `-colonly` node; the spikes are not colliders, exactly as they are not in the pit. THE LETHAL VOLUME IS THE SCENE'S: put an Area3D over this model with a CylinderShape3D radius 1.25 m, height 2.6 m, centred 1.30 m above the model's origin (its roof clears the tallest tip, its floor is the slab), collision_layer 0 and collision_mask 1048577 -- living bodies and ghosts, as scenes/ring/marble.tscn masks SpikeFloor -- handing whatever enters to MatchController.handle_fall(), the way scripts/match/kill_volume.gd does. NOT KillVolume itself: that node writes its own cylinder HANGING BELOW its origin, which is the fall case, not a patch standing on the floor. Godot turns the collider into a StaticBody3D + ConcavePolygonShape3D and drops its mesh, so `surfaces` counts only what is drawn.
